newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Danish Oct CPI seen up, jobless down. [CORRECTED 14:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Danish Oct CPI seen up, jobless down. [CORRECTED 14:50 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects the direction of CPI expectations to up, not down, in headline and text)
Nine Danish bank analysts polled by Reuters on Wednesday forecast higher inflation and lower unemployment rates for October.

Analysts' forecasts averaged 8.3 percent year-on-year unemployment level, down from September's 8.4 percent. CPI was seen up an average 2.4 percent on a year-to-year basis against 2.3 percent in September (corrects from 2.5 percent) using the domestic formula.
There were no CPI forecasts carried out based on the EU formula.
Estimates for October unemployment ranged between 8.2 and 8.4 percent, with CPI forecasts between 2.3 and 2.5 percent.
The Danish national statistics office is scheduled to announce its October CPI and jobless data at 0830 GMT on Thursday, November 28.
